newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour in last-ditch bid to keep sleaze panel.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour in last-ditch bid to keep sleaze panel.

text.p: The Labour party lodged a parliamentary bill on Thursday in a last-gasp attempt to keep the standards and privilges committee sitting until parliament is dissolved on April 8.

There will be no vote on the bill. It will be up to the government to accept or reject the measure on Friday, but Prime Minister John Major earlier said at question time he had no intention of prolonging the life of the committee, which is examining allegations of sleaze against a number of Conservative MPs.
The one-clause bill is sponsored by Labour leader Tony Blair as well as Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown and the leaders of the Scottish and Welsh nationalist parties.
Blair and Ashdown called on Major at question time to act to prolong the life of the committee, whose work will otherwise come to an end on Friday when parliament is prorogued.
Major accused his opponents of a political stunt and said if the committee continued to sit its deliberations would leak, damaging those MPs it is investigating.
